note: Found by the nested parity harness parity/express/nested/jsonwebtoken, which compares the port against jsonwebtoken@9.0.3 case by case. Both findings are cases where the PORT ACCEPTS a token upstream REJECTS, verified against the committed submodule source before being written down. Both are fixed in the express submodule; these entries exist so the released versions get an advisory.

findings.summary: An empty secret is usable: jsonwebtoken.Verify accepts a token forged with a zero-length HMAC key, and Sign mints one
findings.description:
## Summary

`jsonwebtoken.Verify` accepts a token whose HMAC key is zero length, and `Sign`
will mint one. Upstream `jsonwebtoken@9.0.3` refuses both, because `!secretOrPublicKey`
is falsy for an empty string/buffer and it throws `"secretOrPrivateKey must have a value"`.

## Impact

A deployment whose signing secret comes from configuration that resolves to empty
— an unset environment variable, a missing secrets-manager key, a typo'd config
path — does not fail. It silently signs and verifies with a zero-length key, which
every party can reproduce, so anyone can mint an accepted token. Upstream turns the
same misconfiguration into a startup error. The port converts a loud failure into a
silent total authentication bypass.

## Verified against the published module

Reproduced against `github.com/malcolmston/express@v0.4.0` (the latest published
version) with the real v0.4.0 API:

```go
// forge() builds header.payload and HMAC-SHA256s it with the given key.
tok := forge("HS256", []byte(""))
claims, err := jsonwebtoken.Verify(tok, []byte(""))
// => claims non-nil, err == nil   (accepted)
```

## Scope note

This manifest deliberately does NOT contain an algorithm-confusion finding. The
published `jsonwebtoken` package in v0.4.0 is HMAC-only: `SignOptions.Alg` accepts
only HS256/HS384/HS512, and `Verify` rejects a header `alg` of `none`, `RS256` or
lowercase `hs256` outright with "unsupported algorithm" — verified by direct
execution. There is no asymmetric verification path to confuse, so the
public-key-as-HMAC-secret attack does not apply to any released version. That flaw
exists only in the unreleased working tree, where asymmetric support and a
`VerifyOptions.Algorithms` allowlist were added; it was fixed there before release
(`ErrAsymmetricKey`, nil-vs-empty allowlist semantics) and so is not a disclosure.

## Fix

`Sign` and `Verify` now return `ErrMissingKey` for a zero-length key.
